meta.title: Urdu Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 60 letters, signs and pairs · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The Urdu alphabet: 60 notes — the forty letters in the order Urdu primers give them (alif madd beside alif, nūn ġunna beside nūn, the two he's and the two ye's); eight signs a dictionary writes over and under the letters and everyday writing leaves out — zabar, zer and peś for the short vowels, taśdīd, jazm, do zabar, khaṛī zabar and the izāfat; the و that is a short u after خ; and the eleven breathy pairs a consonant makes with do-caśmī he (بھ, پھ … گھ), which a reader meets on every line. The first deck of the Urdu collection. WHAT THE SCRIPT DOES NOT SHOW, since it decides how you study: Urdu writes consonants and long vowels and leaves the short vowels out, so a word cannot be sounded out from its letters alone — of Urdu A1's first 500 headwords 328 have a short vowel no letter shows, and only 89 can be read off the letters with nothing else. That is why every word card in the level decks prints a romanisation beside the word and, where Wiktionary's headword line writes them, the word again with its marks. Learn the letters here; read the vowels there. Urdu is written right to left, and most letters join the next one and change shape as they do, so each card shows the letter alone and then at the start, in the middle and at the end of a word (a letter that never joins the letter after it — ا آ د ڈ ذ ر ڑ ز ژ و — shows two shapes). Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Urdu keeps the spellings of Arabic words with letters that in Urdu sound alike — three s's, four z's, two t's and two h's — so every sound side names its letter, as a speaker does when spelling a word aloud. Every note gives the romanisation the level decks use and one word that shows the letter, a card of the level decks, with a speaker beside the letter and the word (whether it speaks depends on an Urdu voice being installed on your device). THE PACE: the app gives ten new cards a day, both directions together, which is five notes a day, so this deck is 12 days; it can be studied beside Urdu A1 rather than before it, since A1's cards carry their romanisation. The letters are drawn in your device's Urdu typeface, Nastaliq where it has one, in which a word slopes down to the left and a letter's joined shape depends on its neighbours. WHERE THE SOUNDS COME FROM: every English comparison on a sound side is a cell of the column "English approximation" of Wikipedia's key Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu (revision 1367857599), with its bold letters; they are approximations, and several are American English, as the key says. Every phrase between double quotes is a phrase of Wikipedia's article Urdu alphabet (revision 1385216687), as are the letters' names and which letters share a sound. Where the key gives no comparison the card gives none. The example words' romanisations, their marked spellings and their meanings are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0); Wikipedia's text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

fields.Joins: ا ‍ا
fields.Name: الف
fields.Sound: “At the beginning of a word, alif can be used to represent any of the short vowels” (a, i, u); in the middle and at the end of a word it is long ā, the a of father
fields.Example: ابabnow

fields.Joins: آ ‍آ
fields.Name: الف مد
fields.Sound: ā · alif madd: “For long ā at the beginning of words alif-mad is used”: the a of father
fields.Example: آمāmmango

fields.Joins: ب ب‍ ‍ب‍ ‍ب
fields.Name: بے
fields.Sound: b · be: cabbie
fields.Example: بچہbaccachild

fields.Joins: پ پ‍ ‍پ‍ ‍پ
fields.Name: پے
fields.Sound: p · pe: spot — with a breath it is پھ, pot
fields.Example: پانیpānīwater

fields.Joins: ت ت‍ ‍ت‍ ‍ت
fields.Name: تے
fields.Sound: t · te: similar to outthink, Spanish señorita — the dental t
fields.Example: تینtīnthree

fields.Joins: ٹ ٹ‍ ‍ٹ‍ ‍ٹ
fields.Name: ٹے
fields.Sound: ṭ · ṭe: stub (but retroflex) — one of the letters Urdu added “to represent sounds not present in Persian”
fields.Example: ٹکٹṭikaṭticket

fields.Joins: ث ث‍ ‍ث‍ ‍ث
fields.Name: ثے
fields.Sound: s · sun; written se — ث, س and ص are all s
fields.Example: ثابتsābitproven, firm

fields.Joins: ج ج‍ ‍ج‍ ‍ج
fields.Name: جیم
fields.Sound: j · jīm: budging
fields.Example: جگہjagahplace

fields.Joins: چ چ‍ ‍چ‍ ‍چ
fields.Name: چے
fields.Sound: c · che: catch — with a breath it is چھ, beachhead
fields.Example: چائےcāetea

fields.Joins: ح ح‍ ‍ح‍ ‍ح
fields.Name: بڑی حے
fields.Sound: h · ahead; written baṛī he, "big he" — ح and ہ are both h
fields.Example: حصہhissapart, share

fields.Joins: خ خ‍ ‍خ‍ ‍خ
fields.Name: خے
fields.Sound: x · xe: Scottish loch
fields.Example: خوشxuśhappy

fields.Joins: د ‍د
fields.Name: دال
fields.Sound: d · dāl: width, Spanish despacito — the dental d
fields.Example: دنdinday

fields.Joins: ڈ ‍ڈ
fields.Name: ڈال
fields.Sound: ḍ · ḍāl: American bird — the retroflex d, a letter Urdu added
fields.Example: ڈاکٹرḍākṭardoctor

fields.Joins: ذ ‍ذ
fields.Name: ذال
fields.Sound: z · zoo; written zāl — ذ, ز, ض and ظ are all z
fields.Example: ذریعہzariyameans, way

fields.Joins: ر ‍ر
fields.Name: رے
fields.Sound: r · re: American atom; when doubled, Trilled ring
fields.Example: راتrātnight

fields.Joins: ڑ ‍ڑ
fields.Name: ڑے
fields.Sound: ṛ · ṛe: American garter — the retroflex flap, a letter Urdu added
fields.Example: لڑکاlaṛkāboy

fields.Joins: ز ‍ز
fields.Name: زے
fields.Sound: z · zoo; written ze
fields.Example: زبانzabāntongue, language

fields.Joins: ژ ‍ژ
fields.Name: ژے
fields.Sound: ź · źe: pleasure
fields.Example: ٹیلی ویژنṭelī-vīźantelevision

fields.Joins: س س‍ ‍س‍ ‍س
fields.Name: سین
fields.Sound: s · sun; written sīn
fields.Example: سالsālyear

fields.Joins: ش ش‍ ‍ش‍ ‍ش
fields.Name: شین
fields.Sound: ś · śīn: shoe
fields.Example: شہرśahrcity

fields.Joins: ص ص‍ ‍ص‍ ‍ص
fields.Name: صاد
fields.Sound: s · sun; written svād
fields.Example: صبحsubhmorning

fields.Joins: ض ض‍ ‍ض‍ ‍ض
fields.Name: ضاد
fields.Sound: z · zoo; written zvād
fields.Example: ضرورتzarūratneed

fields.Joins: ط ط‍ ‍ط‍ ‍ط
fields.Name: طوئے
fields.Sound: t · similar to outthink, Spanish señorita; written to'e — ت and ط are both the dental t
fields.Example: طرفtarafside, direction

fields.Joins: ظ ظ‍ ‍ظ‍ ‍ظ
fields.Name: ظوئے
fields.Sound: z · zoo; written zo'e
fields.Example: ظاہرzāhirclear, evident

fields.Joins: ع ع‍ ‍ع‍ ‍ع
fields.Name: عین
fields.Sound: ' · 'ain: “in its initial and final position is silent in pronunciation and is replaced by the sound of its preceding or succeeding vowel”
fields.Example: عورت'auratwoman

fields.Joins: غ غ‍ ‍غ‍ ‍غ
fields.Name: غین
fields.Sound: ġ · ġain: Similar to the French R
fields.Example: غلطġalatwrong

fields.Joins: ف ف‍ ‍ف‍ ‍ف
fields.Name: فے
fields.Sound: f · fe: fuss
fields.Example: فونfūnphone

fields.Joins: ق ق‍ ‍ق‍ ‍ق
fields.Name: قاف
fields.Sound: q · qāf: somewhat like caught
fields.Example: قلمqalampen

fields.Joins: ک ک‍ ‍ک‍ ‍ک
fields.Name: کاف
fields.Sound: k · kāf: scab — with a breath it is کھ, cab
fields.Example: کتابkitābbook

fields.Joins: گ گ‍ ‍گ‍ ‍گ
fields.Name: گاف
fields.Sound: g · gāf: ago
fields.Example: گاؤںgāõvillage

fields.Joins: ل ل‍ ‍ل‍ ‍ل
fields.Name: لام
fields.Sound: l · lām: leaf
fields.Example: لالlālred

fields.Joins: م م‍ ‍م‍ ‍م
fields.Name: میم
fields.Sound: m · mīm: much
fields.Example: ماںmā̃mother

fields.Joins: ن ن‍ ‍ن‍ ‍ن
fields.Name: نون
fields.Sound: n · nūn: panther; before g, bang
fields.Example: نامnāmname

fields.Joins: ‍ں
fields.Name: نون غنہ
fields.Sound: “Vowel nasalization is represented by” nūn ġunna, n without its dot, after the vowel: nasal vowel faun; “In middle form nun ghunna is written just like nun”
fields.Example: ہاںhā̃yes

fields.Joins: و ‍و
fields.Name: واؤ
fields.Sound: v · vā'o: the consonant v, vat; or a vowel — ū, cool; o, story; au, off, but long
fields.Example: وقتvaqttime

fields.Joins: ہ ہ‍ ‍ہ‍ ‍ہ
fields.Name: چھوٹی ہے
fields.Sound: h · ahead; written choṭī he, "little he", or gol he; “at the end of a word, it can be used to render the long "a" or the "e" vowels”
fields.Example: ہاتھhāthhand

fields.Joins: ھ ھ‍ ‍ھ‍ ‍ھ
fields.Name: دو چشمی ہے
fields.Sound: h · do-caśmī he, "two-eyed he", is written “in order to create the aspirate consonants”: a breath after the consonant before it — the eleven pairs at the end of this deck
fields.Example: بھائیbhāībrother

fields.Name: ہمزہ
fields.Sound: written alone or above a letter (ئ ؤ ۂ): Urdu writing does “include hamza over bari ye, gol he, and wow”; it is “sometimes pronounced as” a catch — The pause in "uh-oh!"
fields.Example: کئیkaīseveral

fields.Joins: ی ی‍ ‍ی‍ ‍ی
fields.Name: چھوٹی یے
fields.Sound: y · choṭī ye: “It is used for the long vowel "ī" and the consonant "y"”: yuck; seat — and inside a word also e and ai, which at the end of a word are written ے
fields.Example: یادyādmemory

fields.Joins: ‍ے
fields.Name: بڑی یے
fields.Sound: e · baṛī ye, "big ye", “is used to render the vowels "e" and "ai"”: say; fairy — and is told from choṭī ye “only when it comes at the end of a word”
fields.Example: آگےāgeforward

fields.Name: زبر
fields.Sound: a · zabar, the stroke above: short a, about
fields.Example: اَبabnow

fields.Name: زیر
fields.Sound: i · zer, the stroke below: short i, sit
fields.Example: دِنdinday

fields.Name: پیش
fields.Sound: u · peś, the small و above: short u, foot
fields.Example: خُوشxuśhappy

fields.Name: تشدید
fields.Sound: taśdīd, the small w above, “is used to indicate a gemination”: the consonant is doubled
fields.Example: بَچّہbaccachild

fields.Name: جزم
fields.Sound: jazm, the small circle above, “is used to indicate a consonant cluster”: no vowel after the letter
fields.Example: وَقْتvaqttime

fields.Name: دو زبر
fields.Sound: an · do zabar, two zabars (Arabic fathatan), one of the marks “found in some common Arabic loan words”: on the word below it is the -an of fauran
fields.Example: فَوراًfauranimmediately

fields.Name: کھڑی زبر
fields.Sound: ā · khaṛī zabar (Arabic dagger alif), a small alif above, one of the marks found in some common Arabic loan words: on the word below it is the ā of a'lā
fields.Example: اَعْلیٰa'lāgreatest

fields.Name: اضافت
fields.Sound: -e- · izāfat joins two nouns: “A short vowel "i" is used to connect these two words”. It may be written as zer under the last letter of the first word, “but usually is not written at all”; the romanisation writes it -e-
fields.Example: صُورَتِ حالsūrat-e-hālsituation

fields.Name: خو
fields.Sound: xu · و after خ: “Only when preceded by the consonant” xe can vā'o be the short u of foot
fields.Example: خودxudreflexive pronoun: oneself

fields.Name: بھ
fields.Sound: bh · clubhouse
fields.Example: بھائیbhāībrother

fields.Name: پھ
fields.Sound: ph · pot
fields.Example: پھلphalfruit

fields.Name: تھ
fields.Sound: th · Indian English path, birth — the dental t with a breath
fields.Example: تھوڑاthoṛāa little

fields.Name: ٹھ
fields.Sound: ṭh · tub (but retroflex)
fields.Example: ٹھیکṭhīkall right, fine

fields.Name: جھ
fields.Sound: jh · hedgehog
fields.Example: جھوٹjhūṭa lie

fields.Name: چھ
fields.Sound: ch · beachhead
fields.Example: چھوٹاchoṭāsmall

fields.Name: دھ
fields.Sound: dh · adhere (but dental)
fields.Example: دودھdūdhmilk

fields.Name: ڈھ
fields.Sound: ḍh · American birdhouse
fields.Example: ڈھونڈناḍhūnḍnāto look for

fields.Name: ڑھ
fields.Sound: ṛh · no English equivalent, a cross between a voiced retroflex flap and a breathy voiced retroflex plosive.
fields.Example: پڑھناpaṛhnāto read, to study

fields.Name: کھ
fields.Sound: kh · cab
fields.Example: کھاناkhānāfood; to eat

fields.Name: گھ
fields.Sound: gh · loghouse
fields.Example: گھرgharhouse, home
